reason: The cited evidence (E1) reports reduced ductility in NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 at 673–873 K but attributes it to dislocation slip and deformation conditions, not oxidation or grain-boundary embrittlement. No evidence is provided for oxygen diffusion, embrittling oxides, or the role of atmosphere, leaving all key premises unsupported.
premises: Oxygen diffuses preferentially along grain boundaries in HEAs at high temperature
This oxygen diffusion forms embrittling oxides that reduce grain-boundary cohesion
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion promotes intergranular crack propagation and decreases toughness
An inert atmosphere preserves grain-boundary cohesion and retains toughness
